note: Recorded on 2026-08-10 against the Cloud sandbox, unmodified beyond JIRA_RECORD_SCRUB and the response-header filter in transport.KeptHeaders, which drops every header no code reads. `sprint start` against a sprint that already carries both dates, and the reason this file exists: the body is {"state":"active"} and nothing else. Jira requires a sprint to have a window before it will run, and the window belongs to the sprint rather than to the request — so a dated sprint starts from an empty body, and requiring --start and --end unconditionally would refuse a request the server accepts. Both halves are here: the precondition read that finds the sprint future, and the POST that starts it.
